- **A semantic conflict the merge exposed:** 5 of 7 tests in `lathe_post_tormach_thread` failed. Main's PathPilot lathe post (#612) refused any non-zero `FinishAllowance`. Under this PR that field is the finishing pass's own step and is never 0, so every LinuxCNC G76 was refused. Fixed in `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` `g76Why`:
  - LinuxCNC's `R1` ladder (J, 2J, ... clamped at K) has no finish word, but its finishing pass takes the ladder's own last step, `K - (ceil(K/J) - 1)·J`.
  - A record whose finish allowance is that step posts. Any other step is refused by name.
  - An `alternating` record is refused by name.
  - Pinned by the new `g76_takes_the_record_whose_finishing_step_is_the_ladders_own` (1.0 deep in 0.4 rungs: finish 0.2 posts as J0.8 K2.0, and a stated 0.4 is refused) and by an alternating case added to `a_g76_record_the_cycle_cannot_state_exactly_is_refused_by_name`. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`.

**Root cause of TH1 reading Stale after the load: a main defect, not this PR's data.** It reproduces on macOS on plain upstream/main 64506ff5, without this PR or #516.

- `schema::Toolpath::new` computes the path signature (`path_sig::of`) bit-exact from the moves in memory. The program-ahead digest (`rest::prior_digest` -> `digest_of`) reads that signature for every cutting op ahead.
- On save, `project::entity::MoveDto::from_move` snaps every coordinate to the 1 µm lattice. Its doc assumes "generated coordinates are already lattice values".
- When a predecessor's cached path has an off-lattice coordinate, the loaded path differs from the saved one by up to half a micron. Its signature changes, and every op behind it reads Stale ("operation 'X' ahead of it in the program changed").
- Main's radial thread ladder emits off-lattice coordinates whenever its stations or the bar's frame are not lattice numbers. With a 12 TPI lead, TH1 has 12 off-lattice coordinates.
- In your run TH0 used the default (radial) plan. On your platform its frame or stations came out off the lattice. On macOS the 2.0 mm fixture lands exactly on it, which is why #516's refresh could not reproduce the failure.
- A flank, alternating or constant-area plan lands off-lattice on every platform. TH1's alternating plan in this pin has 246 off-lattice coordinates, and its signature changes across the round trip. Nothing follows TH1 in the pin, so the pin itself can only trip through TH0.

Minimal repro on upstream/main (12 TPI, default plan, no #416/#417 code):
1. Build TH1 with `tormach_lathe_support::thread_world_with(false, Right, 25.4/12.0, DEPTH)`.
2. Create TH2 with the same params.
3. Save and load the project.
4. TH2 now reads Stale with "operation 'TH1' ahead of it in the program changed".

This goes to the maintainer to file as its own issue. As asked, I did not patch main's save/digest behaviour in this PR. Candidate fixes are snapping in `Toolpath::new` or hashing lattice-snapped values in `path_sig::of`.

**The pin:** `the_plan_rides_the_project_file_and_a_default_one_is_absent` now also asserts that `rest::prior_digest` of each op is equal before the save and after the load. On a platform where TH0 lands off-lattice, that assert names the defect directly. The plan-change -> Stale behaviour stays pinned in `a_plan_edit_rides_the_history_both_ways`. Until main's fix lands, the pin can still fail on a platform whose libm puts TH0 off the lattice. #516 carries the same pin and the same exposure. It needs no data change of its own, because the fix belongs in main.

**Change** (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, new `g76Allowance`): R is derived from the **rounded** words' own ladder. The post counts the record's rough passes N from its own ladder, rebuilds rungs N-1 and N from the rounded `Q` (first depth), `Q` (minimum depth) and `P` (thread height), and writes the R whose last rough depth `P - R` lies in (rung N-1, rung N], nearest the record's allowance. So the control cuts exactly N rough passes. If that R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance, the cycle is refused by name, with the Q/Q/P words and the R window named. The other G76 words are each one record value rounded once (no differences), so R was the only derived word.

**Golden diff:** only `inch/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`: `G76 P010000 Q157 R0.0157` -> `R0.0158` (control: 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472, the 3 verified passes). The mm goldens are unchanged. Tormach lathe goldens: `git diff upstream/main` is empty.
